title: Lattice Symmetry Remnants in Spatial and Temporal Entanglement of Quantum Critical Spin Chains
abstract: arXiv:2610.31676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum critical lattice models carry universal information beyond the bulk data of their infrared conformal field theory (CFT): microscopic lattice symmetries constrain how the CFT is realized. We probe these remnants through the spatial and temporal entanglement of two Euclidean-evolved states from the same critical model. In the finite-length scaling regime, a conformal boundary encodes the long-distance effect of the short-range initial state, and boundary CFT (BCFT) organizes the universal low-lying entanglement spectrum. We formulate the temporal state as a uniform infinite matrix product state evolved by a symmetry-preserving infinite matrix product operator, using a local factorization regular even at arbitrarily small Trotter steps. For the Ising and three-state Potts chains, whose relevant symmetries are onsite, the spatial and temporal constructions approach the same BCFT structure; varying the initial state engineers conformal boundaries distinguishable spectroscopically. The spin-1/2 XXZ chain instead realizes a Lieb--Schultz--Mattis (LSM) constraint between internal U(1) symmetry and one-site translation. A U(1)-preserving short-range spatial state accommodates it through a doubled unit cell and inequivalent entanglement cuts, whereas the temporal state remains uniform along Euclidean time. Successive spatial transfer steps pump the temporal entanglement spectrum between translation-related Dirichlet sectors, equivalently between integer and half-integer compact-boson zero modes. Breaking U(1) removes both the zero mode and the alternation. Continued evolution at fixed bond dimension crosses over from the finite-length BCFT regime to a finite-entanglement regime generated by symmetry-allowed relevant deformations. Thus microscopic symmetry and anomaly data remain visible in universal entanglement by constraining the boundary realization of the infrared CFT.
summary:
- Lattice symmetries imprint universal signatures on spatial and temporal entanglement spectra of critical spin chains, beyond bulk CFT data.
- Euclidean‑evolved states map to boundary CFTs; changing the short‑range initial state selects distinct conformal boundaries that are spectroscopically distinguishable.
- In the XXZ chain, the Lieb–Schultz–Mattis constraint forces a doubled unit cell in spatial entanglement, while the temporal state stays uniform, leading to pumping between translation‑related Dirichlet sectors.

title: Phonon evidence for a partial, re-entrant spin reorientation near room temperature in LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$
authors: Subha Maity, Dushyant Singh, Vigneshwari S R, Tharundev V V, Navneet Sharma, Subhavenkadesh SS, Krista R. Khiangte
abstract: arXiv:2610.31725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin reorientation near room temperature offers a route to controlling antiferromagnetic order, yet LaFeO$3$, which lacks a magnetic rare-earth ion, is generally expected to retain its spin orientation along the $a$ axis below $T{\mathrm N}\approx740$~K. Here, we investigate LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$ ($x=0$ and 0.1) using temperature-dependent magnetization and Raman spectroscopy over 200--400~K. Both compositions exhibit magnetic anomalies at 285.6 and 323~K, respectively, accompanied by correlated deviations of 12 Raman modes from their conventional anharmonic behavior. Principal component analysis and a global fitting approach reveal a common temperature-dependent phonon response, with mode-dependent amplitudes and signs. To interpret these anomalies, we develop a Landau-based spin-phonon coupling model describing complete, partial re-entrant, and incipient spin reorientation. Comparison with the experimental Raman profiles favors a partial, re-entrant rotation of the N'eel vector in both compositions, centered near 290~K. Ni substitution narrows the characteristic reorientation interval from approximately 116 to 84~K and enhances the magnetization anomaly by a factor of four. An additional feature near 262~K in LaFeO$_3$ is consistent with the Morin transition of trace $\alpha$-Fe$_2$O$_3$. These findings suggest that partial spin reorientation can emerge without magnetic rare-earth ions and establish collective Raman phonon anomalies as a sensitive indirect probe of magnetic anisotropy changes in orthoferrites.
summary:
- Partial, re‑entrant spin reorientation occurs near 290 K in LaFe₁₋ₓNiₓO₃, evidenced by correlated anomalies in magnetization and 12 Raman phonon modes.
- Ni substitution (x = narrows the reorientation temperature window from ~116 K to ~84 K and quadruples the magnetization anomaly.
- The study demonstrates that spin reorientation can arise in a system lacking magnetic rare‑earth ions, with Raman phonon analysis confirming the partial rotation of the Néel vector.

title: Nonadiabatic vibrational dynamics of CO on Pt(111) studied with first-principles many-body perturbation theory
authors: Ra\'ul Bomb\'in, I\~naki Fern\'andez Tena, J. I\~naki Juaristi, Maite Alducin
abstract: arXiv:2610.31727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium vibrational dynamics of CO adsorbed on Pt(111), a prototypical adsorbate-surface system for ultrafast vibrational spectroscopy, using a first-principles framework that combines many-body perturbation theory with density functional theory. Within this methodology we explicitly account for electron-hole pair excitations and electron-mediated phonon-phonon coupling. For the latter mechanism, we evaluate the vertex-correction screening, what constitutes a methodological novelty. Our calculations qualitatively reproduce the transient evolution of the internal stretch vibrational mode observed in femtosecond pump-probe experiments, allowing us to identify in the experimental measurements a small transient blueshift after excitation with a femtosecond laser pulse. As predicted in a previous work, the reduction in the number of electronic states available for electron-phonon coupling when the electronic temperature raises at a group 10 transition metal surface, effectively screens the electron-phonon interaction giving rise to an anomalous transient blue-shift.
summary:
- First‑principles many‑body perturbation theory combined with DFT models nonadiabatic CO vibrational dynamics on Pt(.
- Explicitly includes electron‑hole pair excitations and electron‑mediated phonon‑phonon coupling with vertex‑correction screening.
- Reproduces experimental transient blue‑shift of the CO stretch mode, attributing it to reduced electron‑phonon coupling at elevated electronic temperatures.

title: Altermagnetism in Folded Iron Chain Systems
authors: Ling-Fang Lin, Yang Zhang, Satoshi Okamoto, Adriana Moreo, Lun-Hui Hu, Elbio Dagotto
abstract: arXiv:2610.31732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnetism, a moment-compensated magnetism with momentum-dependent spin splitting, has so far been realized primarily in N\'{e}el-type antiferromagnets. Here, we demonstrate altermagnetism in folded iron-chain systems with block-type magnetic order (e.g., $\uparrow \uparrow \downarrow \downarrow$). In the strictly one-dimensional (1D) case, altermagnetism is forbidden by the $[C_2||{\cal T}]$ symmetry, but it can emerge when such chains are stacked into a quasi-1D array. To generate altermagnetic spin splitting via this chain-stacking mechanism, two essential ingredients are required: a block-type spin order that spontaneously breaks the combined parity-time reversal symmetry, and finite inter-chain hopping. Using first-principles calculations, we identify the K$_3$Fe$_2$Se$_4$ family as a promising platform that realizes this mechanism, hosting a $d$-wave altermagnet even without lattice $C_{4}$ symmetry. Moreover, owing to its lower symmetry, the block-type folded chain exhibits an isotropic altermagnetic spin splitting, which may manifest as an altermagnetic wrapping effect. Our findings unify real-space block magnetism and reciprocal-space altermagnetism, establishing folded iron chains as a tunable platform for zero-moment spintronic applications.
summary:
- Altermagnetism achieved in folded iron chains through block‑type order and inter‑chain hopping, breaking parity‑time symmetry.
- K₃Fe₂Se₄ family hosts a d‑wave, isotropic altermagnetic spin splitting without C₄ symmetry.
- Links real‑space block magnetism with reciprocal‑space altermagnetism, offering a tunable zero‑moment platform for spintronics.

title: Thermoelectric properties and modulation doping of ultrawide-bandgap nitride monolayers
abstract: arXiv:2610.31777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional III-nitride alloys provide a composition-tunable platform for exploring thermoelectric transport and intrinsic electric-field tolerance. We combine first-principles electronic-structure calculations with semiclassical transport for ordered monolayer B$_{x}$Al$_{1-x}$N and B$_{x}$Ga$_{1-x}$N. State-dependent momentum relaxation times computed with AMSET include acoustic deformation-potential and piezoelectric scattering. Using a common, temperature-independent lattice thermal conductivity of 550 W/mK, we predict maximum thermoelectric figure of merit ZT>2.5 for selected p- and n-type monolayers and ZT>2 at 300~K for n-type B$_{0.25}$Ga$_{0.75}$N. Composition-dependent band curvature, screening, and scattering help interpret the different p- and n-type responses. Vacuum-referenced band alignments identify candidate modulation-doping partners for both carrier types; explicit hGaN/V$_2$O$_5$ calculations yield a hole surface density of approximately 1.6$\times10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$. A separate phenomenological model using the band gap and maximum phonon frequency predicts intrinsic breakdown fields of 20.06 and 20.74 MVcm for the Al- and Ga-containing x=0.75 alloys, respectively. These results motivate further investigation for thermoelectric and high-field power-electronic applications. The ZT values apply to the specified scattering and lattice-conductivity models, while the breakdown estimates require validation for monolayers and do not resolve field direction.
summary:
- ZT > 5 predicted for selected p‑ and n‑type BₓAl₁₋ₓN/BₓGa₁₋ₓN monolayers using AMSET scattering and κₗ = 550 W/mK.
- Modulation‑doping partners (e.g., hGaN/V₂O₅) identified, yielding ~6 × 10¹⁴ cm⁻² hole density via band‑alignment analysis.
- Intrinsic breakdown fields ≈ 20 MV

title: Low-energy collective electronic excitations in a gold monolayer
authors: Vyacheslav M. Silkin, Maxim Yu. Kagan
abstract: arXiv:2610.31805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The low-energy plasmonic properties of a free-standing Au(111) monolayer, frequently referred to as goldene, are investigated by time-dependent density functional theory in the random phase approximation. In the evaluation of dielectric and loss functions the first-principle band structure characterized by a single $s-p$ energy band at the Fermi level is taken into account. In this system with apparently simple band structure around the Fermi surface the calculations show the presence, besides the standard two-dimensional (2D) plasmon mode, at even lower energies of three anomalous branches in the momentum-energy region usually assigned to incoherent electron-hole pairs. This is an unexpected result since the electronic system of the gold monolayer is characterized by a single energy band crossing the Fermi level. The dispersion of these anomalous plasmonic branches is strongly anisotropic in-plane and gapless. A general feature is that at small in-plane momentum transfers the modes have a sound-like dispersion in certain momentum directions. We rely the appearance of these anomalous modes to a notable deviation of the Fermi surface of a gold monolayer from a circular shape. As a result of its almost perfect hexagon shape, there is possibility to realize in a {\it single} electronic energy band a scenario of a multi-component electron system with the carrier groups moving with different Fermi velocities in certain momentum directions. The found modes correspond to the out-of-phase charge oscillations of the carriers at different sides of the hexagonal Fermi surface. Hence our work presents evidence how in a metal system with apparently simple band structure around the Fermi level its shape can result in conversion of single-particle charge excitations into collective charge excitations.
summary:
- Goldene monolayer exhibits low‑energy plasmons beyond the standard 2D mode.
- Three gapless, anisotropic plasmon branches appear in the electron‑hole continuum.
- Their sound‑like dispersion arises from the hexagonal Fermi surface, mimicking a multi‑component electron system within a single band.

title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
authors: Ethan Berger, Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Lucas Svensson, Priyanka Deswal, Mehmet Baskurt, Paul Erhart, Julia Wiktor
abstract: arXiv:2610.31830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Perovskites have been studied for a wide range of applications, from oxide-based ferroelectrics to halide-perovskite photovoltaics. Despite their diverse functionalities, these materials share strong lattice anharmonicity arising from structural instabilities such as polar off-centering and octahedral tilting. These anharmonic distortions strongly influence the low-frequency vibrational response and can be observed in infrared (IR) and Raman spectra. However, low-frequency IR and Raman signatures are typically investigated separately, hindering the development of a unified understanding of vibrational spectroscopy across perovskite classes. In this work, we use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate the IR and Raman spectra of oxide perovskites (SrTiO$_3$ and BaTiO$_3$), halide perovskites (CsPbBr$_3$, CsSnBr$_3$, and CsGeBr$_3$) and double halide perovskites (Cs$_2$AgAlBr$_6$ and Cs$_2$AgBiBr$_6$). By comparing materials exhibiting polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities, we find that polar off-centering leads to enhanced low-frequency IR and dielectric responses, whereas nonpolar modes, particularly octahedral tilting, are associated with Raman central peaks. The strength of the low-frequency features also depends on how strongly the underlying modes couple to polarization or dielectric susceptibility. Finally, we show that the dynamics of these instabilities play an important role, with slow polar reorientations shifting the dielectric response to very low frequencies and overdamped tilting modes producing persistent Raman central peaks. These results establish a unified framework connecting low-frequency IR and Raman spectra to the symmetry, coupling and dynamics of their underlying anharmonic lattice instabilities.
summary:
- Unified low‑frequency IR and Raman spectra of oxide, halide, and double‑halide perovskites simulated via machine‑learning MD.
- Polar off‑centering boosts low‑frequency IR/dielectric response; octahedral tilting produces Raman central peaks.
- The intensity of these features depends on mode coupling to polarization/dielectric susceptibility and on the dynamics of the instabilities.

title: Optical signatures of Rashba--Dresselhaus coupling across Franz--Keldysh and Landau regimes in two-dimensional semiconductors
authors: Bahruz Suleymanli, Samir Tariverdiev, B. Tanatar
abstract: arXiv:2610.31843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified theory of the interband optical response of a two-dimensional semiconductor with simultaneous Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit couplings in electric and magnetic fields. In crossed fields, the in-plane electric field generates an effective spin-orbit drift field that modifies the Landau spectrum and spinor states, while at zero magnetic field the problem maps onto Landau--Zener spin dynamics.At zero external fields, the total joint density of states above the band gap remains unchanged, while characteristic subgap structures appear. Pure Rashba coupling produces an inverse square root singularity, whereas a finite Dresselhaus term gives a step and a logarithmic peak, allowing the two couplings to be distinguished optically. At zero magnetic field, the Franz--Keldysh response shows a crossover from diabatic to adiabatic spin dynamics as the electric field is reduced. In the weak-field Rashba regime, the field-free singularity becomes a finite peak whose height scales as $\mathcal E^{-1/3}$ and whose position approaches $E_g-E_{\rm SO}$, providing a direct measure of the Rashba energy. In a perpendicular magnetic field, spin-orbit coupling shifts and splits the Landau absorption lines and produces anticrossings without changing their total weights. The Rashba splitting changes from a $\sqrt{B}$ dependence at weak fields to a linear dependence at strong fields. Finally, in crossed electric and magnetic fields, the electric field broadens the Landau lines and drives a continuous crossover toward the Franz--Keldysh regime, while spin-orbit coupling produces opposite shifts and different widths for the two members of each doublet.
summary:
- Unified theory of interband optical response in 2D semiconductors with simultaneous Rashba–Dresselhaus SOC under crossed electric and magnetic fields.
- Zero‑field subgap signatures: Rashba yields an inverse‑square‑root singularity; Dresselhaus adds a step and logarithmic peak, allowing optical discrimination of the two couplings.
- Field‑dependent behavior: Franz–Keldysh crossover from diabatic to adiabatic spin dynamics; Rashba splitting changes from √B at weak B to linear at strong B; Landau absorption lines shift, split, and anticross without altering total weight.

title: 'Dancing' two-dimensional patterns in nematics above the flexoelectric instability threshold
abstract: arXiv:2610.31849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Various types of electrohydrodynamic instabilities in liquid crystals (LCs) are a recurring theme in LC research. The nonlinear stage of the flexoelectric instability in nematics remains the least studied aspect of this phenomenon. This work highlights a key advancement in nonlinear physics, providing a compelling example of nonlinear dynamical system behavior. By solving the system of nonlinear equations for a nematic in an alternating external field, we derive from first principles the unique "dancing" behavior of truly two-dimensional patterns above the flexoelectric instability threshold. Our analysis is restricted to liquid crystals with negative dielectric permittivity and electrical conductivity anisotropies. The resulting solution represents a stable limit cycle near above the Hopf bifurcation, valid within the parameters range where the solutions characteristic exponent is complex. The generalized two-dimensional Ginzburg-Landau-like phenomenological theory of the phenomenon is developed.
summary:
- Shows “dancing” 2‑D patterns in nematics above the flexoelectric threshold by solving nonlinear equations.
- Finds a stable limit cycle near a Hopf bifurcation for LCs with negative dielectric and conductivity anisotropies.
- Develops a generalized 2‑D Ginzburg–Landau phenomenological theory for the phenomenon.

title: Strontium Titanate Capping Layers as Kinetic Regulators of Redox Phase Transitions in Oxide Heterostructures
authors: Pooya Abdollahi, Woo Jin Kim, Keaghan Knight, Harold Y. Hwang, Ambrose Seo
abstract: arXiv:2610.31871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oxide capping layers are widely used to protect and stabilize thin-film heterostructures, yet their role in governing phase-transition kinetics remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover the kinetic function of few-nanometer-thick SrTiO$_3$ (STO) capping layers in controlling oxidation and reduction processes, using real-time in situ optical spectroscopic ellipsometry. We show that oxygen diffusion through the nanoscale capping layer constitutes the rate-limiting step, giving rise to diffusion-controlled phase transitions in the underlying materials. As a result, both capping-layer thickness and oxygen partial pressure provide effective handles to tune phase transition temperatures. Quantitative analysis yields an activation energy of $E_A$ = 0.64 $\pm$0.06 eV for oxygen diffusion through STO, highlighting its suitability for precise control of redox reactions in diverse material systems. These results establish oxide capping layers as active kinetic regulators of redox-driven phase transitions and offer a general framework for engineering redox dynamics in complex oxide heterostructures.
summary:
- SrTiO₃ capping layers (few nm) limit oxygen diffusion, making it the rate‑limiting step for redox phase transitions in underlying oxides.
- Capping‑layer thickness and ambient O₂ partial pressure tune transition temperatures, enabling precise kinetic control.
- Measured activation energy for O₂ diffusion through STO is 64 ± 06 eV, confirming its effectiveness as a kinetic regulator.

title: Kinetic competition controls loss-induced exceptional points of Hubbard pairs
abstract: arXiv:2610.32123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-body loss can bind two fermions in a Hubbard lattice, yet the binding threshold in the infinite lattice need not be an exceptional point (EP). At fixed total momentum $\mathbf{K}$, the hops of the two particles interfere into a relative-motion hopping along each lattice direction, which sets the kinetic energy of the relative motion. On a hypercubic lattice, the threshold $g_c=1/[\pi\rho_2(0)]$ is an EP precisely when the maximum kinetic energy along one direction exceeds the sum of the transverse maxima. This dominance keeps every transverse-momentum scattering channel propagating near the band center, making the local pair Green function purely imaginary there. Two real-energy scattering zeros associated with coherent perfect absorption then coalesce at the threshold into a second-order EP of the analytically continued pair problem, where loss restores the parity-time symmetry of the pair's scattering solutions. Without a dominant direction, binding occurs without coalescence and without breaking of that symmetry. Total momentum can therefore select EP sectors even on isotropic lattices. More broadly, the kinetic structure of the two-particle continuum determines whether loss-induced binding and exceptional degeneracy coincide.
summary:
- Two‑body loss can bind fermions in a Hubbard lattice, with a binding threshold \(g_c=1/[\pi\rho_2(]\).
- The threshold becomes an exceptional point when the kinetic energy along one lattice direction dominates the transverse directions, making the pair Green function purely imaginary at the band center.
- This kinetic competition allows total momentum to select EP sectors, restoring parity‑time symmetry of the scattering solutions and linking loss‑induced binding to exceptional degeneracy.

title: Compass Correlations in a Square-Lattice Magnet
authors: Otkur Omar, Matthias D. Frontzek, Gabriele Sala, Junying Shen, Xinmin Wang, Ze Hu, Zhuang Xu, Zecong Qin, Xin Tong, Joe Paddison, Max Hirschberger, Shinichiro Seki, Masaaki Matsuda, Matthew B. Stone, Andrew D. Christianson, Nguyen D. Khanh, Shang Gao
abstract: arXiv:2610.32157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The square-lattice compass model is a paradigm of bond-dependent frustration, yet experimental evidence for its characteristic spin correlations has remained elusive. Here we identify compass correlations in the square-lattice intermetallic ErRu$_2$Si$_2$ using single-crystal neutron diffuse scattering. Comparative measurements on the isostructural compounds NdRu$_2$Si$_2$ and ErRu$_2$Si$_2$ reveal a pronounced contrast between nearly uniform diffuse rings in the former and strong intensity modulation between Brillouin zones in the latter. Through the magnetic neutron polarization factor, this modulation reveals compass correlations that couple moment orientation to the correlation wavevector. Crystal-field spectroscopy identifies four preferred in-plane orientations for the Er$^{3+}$ moments. A minimal compass-Heisenberg model incorporating this anisotropy quantitatively reproduces the diffuse scattering and accounts for the double-$Q$ vortex-antivortex ground state. Fits with the compass couplings fixed at values set by the dipolar energy scale retain good agreement with the data, supporting a substantial dipolar contribution to the bond-dependent interactions. Our results establish a square-lattice platform for compass physics and suggest that dipolar interactions, acting together with local crystal-field anisotropy, can shape directional magnetic correlations alongside conduction-electron-mediated exchange.
summary:
- Compass correlations observed in ErRu₂Si₂ via neutron diffuse scattering, unlike uniform rings in NdRu₂Si₂.
- Four in‑plane easy axes identified; a compass‑Heisenberg model reproduces scattering and predicts a double‑Q vortex‑antivortex ground state.
- Dipolar interactions, together with crystal‑field anisotropy, drive the bond‑dependent correlations on the square lattice.

title: Intrinsic Paramagnetism of Optical Phonons and Thermal Hall Effect in Quantum Paraelectrics
authors: Harsh Jain, Manideep Gone, Nabyendu Das
abstract: arXiv:2610.32224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a microscopic theory of the phonon-mediated thermal Hall effect in quantum paraelectrics, driven by the intrinsic paramagnetism due to quantum fluctuations of the (nearly) critical optical phonon modes. The effective magnetization due to temporal fluctuations of the assosciated dipoles couple to an external magnetic field resulting the magnetoelectric term $\mathbf{H} \cdot (\mathbf{P} \times \dot{\mathbf{P}})$ in the effective Lagrangian density of the polarisation field $\mathbf{P}$. This coupling splits the transverse optical phonon spectrum into right- and left-circularly polarized chiral branches. Using the chiral phonon Green's functions and the Kubo formalism, we derive the thermal Hall conductivity $\kappa_{xy}$ from the heat-current correlation function. We observe that $\kappa_{xy}$ is proportional to the difference in spectral weights of the two chiral modes, $\kappa_{xy} \propto A_+^2 - A_-^2$, establishing a direct microscopic link between phonon chirality and transverse heat transport. Our theory predicts three key observations: (i) a linear-in-magnetic-field response $\kappa_{xy} \propto H$ at low fields, evolving into nonlinear behavior at higher fields (ii) a non-monotonic temperature dependence of $\kappa_{xy}$ with a peak arising from the competition between thermal population and phonon scattering and (iii) strong enhancement of $\kappa_{xy}$ near the quantum critical point $\omega_0 \to 0$, it exhibits power-law scaling $\kappa_{xy} \propto T^{\alpha}$ with $\alpha \approx 0.41$. Our findings provide an understanding of thermal Hall transport in quantum paraelectrics due to intrinsic paramagnetism and is aligned with the observed behaviour in SrTiO$_3$ and related materials.

title: Triplon dynamics from partial Kondo screening in frustrated heavy-fermion systems
authors: Hiroki Nakahara, Masahito Mochizuki, Rintaro Eto
abstract: arXiv:2610.32283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The partially disordered (PD) phase, in which magnetically ordered and Kondo-screened sites coexist, has been proposed as a possible ground state of geometrically frustrated heavy-fermion systems. We investigate its dynamical properties in the half-filled periodic Anderson model on a triangular lattice by calculating the dynamical spin susceptibility within the random-phase approximation built on a self-consistent Hartree-Fock solution. We show that successive quantum phase transitions from the Kondo-insulating phase to the PD phase and to a magnetically ordered phase are driven by the condensation of triplon modes originating predominantly from the Kondo-screened sites. In the PD phase, magnons and triplons coexist and hybridize, leading to characteristic level repulsion in the excitation spectrum. These results reveal how triplet excitations evolve into collective magnetic modes across the successive phase transitions and highlight the dynamical interplay between magnetic order and Kondo screening in frustrated heavy-fermion systems.
summary:
- Triplon condensation triggers successive transitions: Kondo insulator → partially disordered → magnetic order.
- In the PD phase, magnons and triplons coexist and hybridize, causing level repulsion in the spectrum.
- RPA on self‑consistent Hartree–Fock shows how triplet excitations evolve into collective magnetic modes.

title: Low-Temperature Hybrid Monte Carlo for Perylene and Corannulene: Stabilizing Determinant and Force
authors: Petar Sinilkov, Thomas Luu, Johann Ostmeyer, Finn L. Temmen, Marcel Rodekamp
abstract: arXiv:2610.32378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate a real world physics study of the molecules perylene and corannulene at different doping levels, and calculating selected one-, two- (exciton) and three-body (trion) correlators. This has been done by performing Hubbard-model simulations near room temperature. We find, between charge neutral and doubly charged plateaus of perylene, an interaction-induced $\Delta Q = 1$ plateau whose width grows with interaction strength and in which the ground state is a spin doublet rather than a singlet. The algorithmic advancement enabling this study simultaneously stabilizes the determinant and force calculations to machine precision at room temperature, while scaling as well as standard determinant Quantum Monte Carlo simulations of these systems. Furthermore, our formalism retains the full time-displaced (2-point) Green's function, allowing us to construct any $n$-body correlator, including those that contain disconnected diagrams.
summary:
- Hubbard‑model simulations of perylene and corannulene at various dopings, computing 1‑, 2‑ (exciton) and 3‑body (trion) correlators.
- Discovery of an interaction‑induced ΔQ = 1 plateau in perylene, with a spin‑doublet ground state.
- New hybrid Monte Carlo algorithm stabilizes determinant and force calculations to machine precision at room temperature while retaining full time‑displaced Green’s functions for arbitrary n‑body correlators.

title: Hybrid Monte Carlo for the extended Kane-Mele-Hubbard model
authors: Finn L. Temmen, Thomas Luu, Johann Ostmeyer, Lin Wang
abstract: arXiv:2610.32458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Hubbard model offers a powerful minimal description of strongly correlated electrons in molecules and materials, yet it neglects effects observed in nature that give rise to a much richer variety of physics. For instance, including nonlocal interactions introduces a competition between strongly correlated phases, while incorporating spin-orbit coupling (SOC) can lead to the emergence of exotic topological phases. Seeking a more realistic platform for simulating graphene and, potentially, related materials such as transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), we therefore consider the extended Kane-Mele-Hubbard model, which features a Kane-Mele SOC term and nearest-neighbor interactions. Simulating this model is particularly challenging once the nonlocal interactions become dominant over the on-site Hubbard interaction, as a severe sign problem arises already at half filling, leaving this regime largely unexplored. In this work, we develop continuous auxiliary field formulations of the model, suitable for treatment with the Hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) algorithm. Using these formulations, we characterize the sign problem across the model's parameter space and establish where simulations are feasible, as a first step toward the full phase diagram.
summary:
- Developed continuous auxiliary‑field formulations for the extended Kane‑Mele‑Hubbard model, enabling Hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) simulations.
- Mapped the sign problem across the model’s parameter space, pinpointing regimes where HMC is feasible.
- Established groundwork for exploring the full phase diagram of graphene‑like systems with nonlocal interactions and spin‑orbit coupling.

title: Discrete WKB approach to density profiles in inhomogeneous two-band free-fermion chains
authors: Federico Finkel, Artemio Gonz\'alez-L\'opez, Mart\'in Zapata
abstract: arXiv:2610.32710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the discrete WKB method to one-dimensional bipartite tight-binding chains of free fermions with slowly varying hopping amplitudes and on-site potentials. We focus on the inhomogeneous Rice-Mele model, suggesting possible experimental realizations thereof in optical superlattices. We derive explicit semiclassical expressions for the single-particle wave functions and density of states, as well as the sublattice-resolved local particle densities and filling fraction at arbitrary Fermi energy. In particular, we show that the WKB density profiles agree with those obtained from the local-density approximation. We analyze the spatial dependence of the local band edges and its consequences for the global spectral structure, and clarify the role played by the phase-space topology in determining the Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization conditions. Finally, we illustrate our results with two representative examples: a homogeneous Rice-Mele chain subject to a harmonic trap and a fully inhomogeneous chain containing a domain wall.

title: Tensor Networks for Materials Simulation and Quantum Chemistry
authors: Saeed S. Jahromi, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Roman Rausch, Sukhbinder Singh, Roman Orus
abstract: arXiv:2610.32754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting the properties of correlated materials and molecules often requires a many-body description that goes beyond single-particle and mean-field approximations. Tensor networks address this challenge by exploiting the entanglement structure of quantum states to construct compact, systematically improvable representations. Although developed largely for idealized model Hamiltonians, these methods are increasingly being integrated into material-specific calculations. This Perspective introduces their underlying principles and examines how network geometry, bond-dimension truncation, and approximate contraction determine the accuracy and computational reach of these approaches. We survey applications across regimes of increasing complexity, ranging from ground-state properties of quantum magnets and itinerant-fermion systems to excitation spectra, nonequilibrium dynamics, finite-temperature and open systems, and molecular electronic structure. We then examine four routes connecting these methods to real materials, including experimentally constrained models, downfolded Hamiltonians, dynamical mean-field theory with tensor network impurity solvers, and quantum embedding. Throughout, we evaluate the maturity of existing capabilities and their principal limitations, synthesizing this assessment into a practical method-selection guide. We argue that reliable materials predictions require quantifying uncertainties introduced at each stage, from constructing material-specific Hamiltonians to extracting experimentally accessible observables. Finally, we identify the algorithmic advances and reproducible computational practices needed to establish tensor networks as a routine tool for predictive materials science and quantum chemistry.
summary:
- Tensor networks offer compact, entanglement‑based many‑body representations for correlated materials and molecules.
- Accuracy hinges on network geometry, bond‑dimension truncation, and contraction approximations, impacting ground‑state, excitation, dynamics, and finite‑temperature studies.
- Four practical integration routes—experimentally constrained models, downfolded Hamiltonians, DMFT with tensor‑network solvers, and quantum embedding—are evaluated with a maturity guide.

title: Unconventional charge density wave order in ErTe$_{3}$: symmetry breakings and fluctuations probed by Raman scattering
authors: Th\'eotime Freitas, Mattia Udina, Alexandr Alekhin, Niloufar Nilforoushan, Sarah Houver, Alain Sacuto, Benito A. Gonzalez, Ian R. Fisher, Indranil Paul, Yann Gallais
abstract: arXiv:2610.32797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent experiments have revealed unexpected mirror-symmetry breakings in the charge density-wave (CDW) state of rare-earth tritellurides, suggesting a putative ferro-axial CDW state. Here we report polarization-resolved Raman scattering measurements tracking the point-group symmetry breakings across the CDW phase transition in the rare-earth tritelluride ErTe$_3$. We show that the mirror-symmetry breakings follow closely the emergence of the CDW order, suggesting a single component CDW order parameter. Furthermore, Raman measurements in the $A_{2g}$ symmetry channel above the CDW transition temperature indicate the absence of significant ferro-axial fluctuations. We discuss the broad implications of these findings with respect to the nature of the CDW state in the tritellurides.
summary:
- Mirror‑symmetry breaking appears simultaneously with CDW onset, implying a single‑component order parameter.
- Polarization‑resolved Raman scattering maps point‑group symmetry changes across the CDW transition.
- No significant ferro‑axial fluctuations are observed above T_CDW in the A₂g symmetry channel.
